effects.log: You eat half. The fear goes; the care stays. {npc} pats the next dog carefully, from the side, and is not bitten. (Rice +2)

events.text: A master has come to duel you and stays to ask for a blade back: {npc}, whose grandmother's sword is somewhere in you. "It is no use to you," says {npc}. "It is a family's."

choices.text: Give it back

effects.log: You find it among the others, and give it back, with your toothmarks on the guard. {npc} holds it for a long time and says the toothmarks will be part of it now. (Rice +3)

choices.text: Duel for it, as {he} came to

ok.log: You duel, gently, and win, and give it back anyway. {npc} cannot decide whether to be grateful or furious, and settles on both. (Rice +2)

fail.log: {npc} wins, fairly, and you give it back, as the duel said. {npc} looks at it and says it was worth the trip. (-4 health, Rice +2)

events.text: {npc}, a monk general of an old order, stands before you with a plain old staff in {his} hands. "I could stop you," {npc} says. "My teachers taught me how. I would rather you came and helped us rebuild the temples the war burned."

choices.text: Go and help rebuild

effects.log: You go, and carry beams up mountains for years, and give the temples their bells back out of your Belly. {npc} never raises the staff. (Rice +3)

choices.text: Ask to see the staff first

effects.log: {npc} lets you see it. It is a good staff, and an old one, worn at the grip. You go and help rebuild anyway, because you liked being asked. (Rice +2)

events.text: A company of soldiers comes up the valley and looses arrows at you, because somebody at court still has an order on a scroll that says to, and nobody has ever crossed it out. The arrows break on your hide like straws.

choices.text: Eat the arrowheads and send them home

effects.log: You eat the arrowheads off the grass and send the soldiers home with their bows. The captain salutes you, which is not in the order, either.

choices.text: Ask the captain to get the order crossed out

effects.log: You ask the captain, kindly, to get the order crossed out. The captain says it would take a minister. You say you will wait. You wait a long time. The order comes back next spring all the same.

choices.text: Lie still and let them run out of arrows

effects.log: You lie still. They run out of arrows by noon. They go home. Nobody is hurt, which you notice the soldiers are glad of.

events.text: Fire-arrows, this time: a young officer who has read the old books and wants to be the one who finds the tail. The arrows come down in a burning rain around your hill.

choices.text: Eat the fire out of the air

effects.log: You eat the fire out of the air before it lands. The young officer stands there with an empty quiver and a great deal to think about. (Heat +10)

choices.text: Curl your tail under you and wait

effects.log: You curl your tail under you and wait for the arrows to run out. They do. One scorches a needle on your flank. You do not even feel it.

events.text: The smiths of three valleys have come up together with a petition, read out by the eldest from a sheet held at arm's length: there is not enough iron in the land to make ploughs, because a great deal of it is in you.

choices.text: Give them iron for a generation of ploughs

effects.log: You give them iron for a generation of ploughs, in the smiths' yards, at dawn. The petition is framed in three valleys. (Rice +2)

choices.text: Give them a little, and promise more

effects.log: You give them a little, and promise more when the harvest is bad. The smiths say that is fair, mostly. (Rice +1)

choices.text: Tell them to dig the mountains

effects.log: You tell them to dig the mountains, as you did. The smiths go home and dig. It is hard, and they are angry at you for a decade, and then they have a mine. (Rice -1)

events.text: A village has left broken iron at its gate for you: cracked pots, bent hoes, a rusted lock, nails pulled out of a house that fell in the rains. A child has written on a board, in a careful hand: for the Iron-Eater, please eat our bad luck too.

choices.text: Eat it, and the bad luck

effects.log: You eat it, and lie outside the gate a night and eat the village's bad dreams as well, which is what bad luck mostly is. (Rice +2)

choices.text: Eat it, and leave a good plough in its place

effects.log: You eat it and leave a good plough at the gate in its place. The child who wrote the board finds it in the morning and runs the whole village round to see. (Rice +2)

events.text: A bounty hunter creeps through the reeds toward you at night, with salt, a whip and a burning torch, sure of the old books. You are awake. You are always awake now, a little.

choices.text: Eat the torch out of the hunter's hand

effects.log: You lean over and eat the torch, flame and all, and then the whip, and then, after a moment's thought, the salt pot's iron lid. The hunter sits down in the reeds and laughs, helplessly, at the end of a career.

choices.text: Ask the hunter what the bounty is

effects.log: You ask. The hunter tells you, sheepishly. It is not much. You give the hunter a famous general's dagger worth ten bounties, and the hunter goes home rich and never hunts again. (Rice +1)

events.text: A delegation of Mount Hua's disciples kneels in the road in front of you. They do not ask for the plum-blossom sword outright. They only say that the founder's hall is empty, and the disciples do not know what to bow to.
events.arc: A Sect Wants Its Sword Back

choices.text: Give it back

effects.log: You give it back, toothmarks and all. Later, if they want, they may give it again, freely, and that will count. They carry it home in a procession, and the founder's hall is full again. (Back to its heirs. Rice +3)

choices.text: Keep it, and tell them to bow to the empty place

effects.log: You tell them to bow to the empty place. It is the founder's too. They go home angry, and bow to it, and in a generation it is the most famous empty place in the murim. (Rice -1)

events.text: A delegation of Wudang's Taoists kneels in the road in front of you. They do not ask for the taiji sword outright. They only say that the founder's hall is empty, and the disciples do not know what to bow to.
events.arc: A Sect Wants Its Sword Back

choices.text: Give it back

effects.log: You give it back, toothmarks and all. Later, if they want, they may give it again, freely, and that will count. They carry it home in a procession, and the founder's hall is full again. (Back to its heirs. Rice +3)

choices.text: Keep it, and tell them to bow to the empty place

effects.log: You tell them to bow to the empty place. It is the founder's too. They go home angry, and bow to it, and in a generation it is the most famous empty place in the murim. (Rice -1)

events.text: A delegation of Shaolin's monks kneels in the road in front of you. They do not ask for the iron staff outright. They only say that the rack in the founder's hall is empty, and the disciples do not know what to bow to.
events.arc: A Sect Wants Its Sword Back

choices.text: Give it back

effects.log: You give it back, toothmarks and all. Later, if they want, they may give it again, freely, and that will count. They carry it home in a procession, and the rack in the founder's hall is full again. (Back to its heirs. Rice +3)

choices.text: Keep it, and tell them to bow to the empty place

effects.log: You tell them to bow to the empty place. It is the founder's too. They go home angry, and bow to it, and in a generation it is the most famous empty place in the murim. (Rice -1)

events.text: A delegation of the Martial Alliance's elders kneels in the road in front of you. They do not ask for the Leader's sword outright. They only say that the Leader's hall is empty, and the disciples do not know what to bow to.
events.arc: A Sect Wants Its Sword Back

choices.text: Give it back

effects.log: You give it back, toothmarks and all. Later, if they want, they may give it again, freely, and that will count. They carry it home in a procession, and the Leader's hall is full again. (Back to its heirs. Rice +3)

choices.text: Keep it, and tell them to bow to the empty place

effects.log: You tell them to bow to the empty place. It is the founder's too. They go home angry, and bow to it, and in a generation it is the most famous empty place in the murim. (Rice -1)

events.text: Someone in the valley has left a bowl of rice at the foot of a chimney for you, on a roof tile, with a spoon of good brass beside it, because it is a cold winter and the children have been having bad dreams.

choices.text: Eat the rice, leave the spoon, eat the dreams

effects.log: You eat the rice. You leave the spoon. You lie by the chimney till dawn eating what comes down the flue. The children sleep till noon. (Rice +2)

choices.text: Eat the rice and the spoon

effects.log: You eat both. Somebody in the house sees, and tells everyone, and next winter there are two spoons. (Rice +1)

events.text: In the river villages where you once ate bad dreams, the bowl at the chimney is a custom now. On the coldest night of the year there is one at every house, and you cannot possibly eat them all.

choices.text: Eat one at every house, all night

effects.log: You try. You eat one at every house, all night, walking the length of the river. At dawn you have eaten eight hundred bowls of rice and you are, for once, not hungry. (Rice +4)

choices.text: Eat one, and leave the rest for the poor

effects.log: You eat one, and lie in the main street so that everyone knows you have come, and the rest of the bowls go to the people who need them more. The towns say this is what you meant all along. (Rice +2)

events.text: A village where everyone is having the same bad dream: a flood, a fire, a war, it changes. Something is wrong with the village, and the dream is how it is wrong.

choices.text: Eat the dream, house by house

effects.log: You eat it, house by house, all night. It comes back the next night, weaker, and you eat it again, and on the third night it does not come. (Rice +3)

choices.text: Look for what the dream is about

effects.log: You look, and find it: a well dug where a grave was, long ago. You tell the elders. They fill the well and dig another, and the dream stops by itself. (Rice +2)

events.text: An old soldier in a hut on the hillside has dreamed of the same battle every night for fifty years. The village has asked you to come, very shyly, as if it were a great deal to ask.

choices.text: Eat the battle

effects.log: You lie outside the hut and eat the battle, the whole of it, the shouting and the smoke. In the morning the old soldier comes out and says the dream was of a wife's face instead, the first time in fifty years. (Rice +3)

choices.text: Eat most of it, and leave the friends

effects.log: You eat the battle but leave the friends who were in it, so the old soldier can still see them at night, without the smoke. (Rice +2)

events.text: An old master nobody has heard of comes down the path with a plain sword, the only one there is, and holds it out hilt-first. "It has never been famous," the master says. "It has kept a village safe for forty years. That should be enough."

choices.text: Take it, as given

effects.log: You take it. It is enough. It counts for as much as the plum-blossom blade, and the old master goes home whistling. (Rice +2)

choices.text: Ask who will keep the village safe now

effects.log: You ask. The master grins and says: you will, now. Fair. You send down a hundred ploughs and a temple bell to the village, and lie near it a winter. (Rice +3)

events.text: A swordswoman who fought you long ago and lost comes back very old and gives you the sword she fought you with. "I always meant to," she says. "I was too proud. I am not proud any more."

choices.text: Take it, as given

effects.log: You take it. She sits down beside you and tells you about the fight, every move of it; she remembers it better than you do. (Rice +2)

choices.text: Tell her the fight was hers

effects.log: You tell her the fight was hers, really; you only had more iron. She laughs, and says that is the kindest lie anyone has told her, and gives you the sword anyway. (Rice +3)

events.text: The children from the valley are climbing you, using the hilts on your back as a ladder, daring each other to touch your ear.

choices.text: Twitch the ear

effects.log: You twitch the ear. Eleven children scream with joy and slide down your side all at once into the grass. They will be back tomorrow.

choices.text: Hold perfectly still

effects.log: You hold perfectly still. The bravest one touches your ear and sits there, on the top of the world, very quiet, looking at the sea. (Rice +1)

events.text: A child has got stuck halfway up your flank, between two hilts, and is too proud to call for help, and too frightened to move.

choices.text: Lift the child down with your trunk

effects.log: You lift the child down, slowly, and set the child in the grass. The child says nobody is to know. Nobody does, except everyone who was watching.

choices.text: Lift the child up to the top instead

effects.log: You lift the child up to the top instead. The child sits on your head, stops being frightened at all, and refuses to come down until supper. (Rice +1)

events.text: You are passing the ridge with the old mine under it, where you slept when you were small enough to fit. The entrance is far too small for you now. You can smell the seam.

choices.text: Put your trunk in and gnaw a little

effects.log: You put your trunk in and gnaw the seam, very gently, the way you did. Dead iron, nobody poorer. It tastes like being young.

choices.text: Lie at the entrance and sleep a long while

effects.log: You lie down across the entrance and sleep for years. Pines grow a little on your back. The village below forgets you are a beast and starts calling you a hill again.

events.text: A monsoon decade. It rains all summer every summer, and rust runs off you in orange streams into the paddies, and the farmers below say the rice tastes of iron, and is very good for the blood.

choices.text: Shelter under a cliff

effects.log: You shelter under a cliff until the rains end. You are a little smaller. Iron does not make you more any more; it does not make you less much, either.

choices.text: Lie out in it and let the paddies have what runs off

effects.log: You lie out in it. The paddies below you have the best harvests in the province, and nobody knows why but the frogs. (Rice +1)

events.text: In a market lane a grandmother is scolding a child who will not stop eating: "Like Songdo's Iron-Eater, you are!" All these years, and you are still a proverb.

choices.text: Stand very still at the end of the lane

effects.log: You stand at the end of the lane, very still. The grandmother sees you, and does not drop the scolding, which you respect. The child sees you and stops eating at once.

choices.text: Walk on, a little ashamed

effects.log: You walk on, a little ashamed. It is a fair proverb. You give back a plough in the next village, for the proverb's sake. (Rice +1)

events.text: Winter in the palace garden. The underfloor fires are lit, and the sparks come up out of the brick chimneys, and you come down from the hills, as you always do, to eat them before they land.

choices.text: Eat the sparks all winter

effects.log: You eat the sparks all winter. Not one roof catches. The palace staff leave you a bowl of rice on the terrace on the coldest night, without being told. (Rice +2)

choices.text: Visit your own carving first

effects.log: You visit the little carving at the foot of the chimney first, and lie beside it, and look at it, and think it has got fatter. (Rice +1)

choices.text: Lie at the foot of the chimney first, and listen to the palace

effects.log: You lie at the foot of the chimney first, and listen to the palace settling for the night: the ladies, the watchmen, the sparks ticking in the flue. (Rice +1)

events.text: A swordsman blocks the road with a drawn blade. They have heard that the Iron-Eater cannot be killed and want to see for themselves. They are quite good, and quite young, and quite certain.

choices.text: Fight, gently

ok.log: You fight, gently, and at the end you have the blade in your jaws and the swordsman on the ground, laughing. You give it back with your toothmarks on the guard. It will be a famous sword one day because of them.

fail.log: The swordsman lands a cut you feel, and stands back amazed. You laugh. They go away with a story nobody believes. (-4 health)

choices.text: Lie down in the road and wait

effects.log: You lie down in the road. The swordsman waits for you to attack. You do not. After an hour, embarrassed, they put the sword away and walk round you.

events.text: The fever has come back to a river town, as fevers do, and the straw ropes are up across the doors again.

choices.text: Lie across the main road and eat it

effects.log: You lie across the main road and eat it, all one night and the next. The ropes come down in a fortnight. (Rice +3, -5 health)

choices.text: Send for the physicians and eat what they cannot cure

effects.log: You send word to the physicians in the capital, and eat what they cannot cure, and between you the town loses only a few. (Rice +2)

events.text: A smith in the valley has found an old mould for a sword in the back of the forge, and cannot remember what it is for. Nobody in the village can. It is passed round at the market as a curiosity, and a child says it looks like a very thin plough.

choices.text: Tell them what it was

effects.log: You tell them, in the voice of a swordsmith you ate long ago. They listen politely, as to a grandparent's story about wolves. The smith makes a very thin plough out of it, which works well in stony ground.

choices.text: Let them forget

effects.log: You let them forget. It is the best thing that has happened in the valley in a thousand years, and nobody knows it but you. (Rice +2)

events.text: A whole generation has grown up in the valley that has never seen a real sword drawn in anger. The sects still teach the forms, with wood. The forms are very beautiful. They are a kind of dance now, and the old masters are not sure whether to be proud or ashamed.

choices.text: Tell the masters to be proud

effects.log: You tell them to be proud. The forms were always the beautiful part. The masters argue about it for a decade and decide you are right, mostly. (Rice +1)

choices.text: Watch the dance at the spring festival

effects.log: You watch the forms at the spring festival, a hundred disciples with wooden swords moving like water, and the whole valley watching you watch. You sleep well that year.

events.text: A festival in the valley is named for you now: one day in spring when every family brings one broken thing of iron to your feet, and you eat it, and the bad luck of the year goes with it. The children wear paper trunks.

choices.text: Eat every broken thing, slowly, with ceremony

effects.log: You eat every broken thing, one at a time, with great ceremony, while the children in paper trunks march round you. It takes all day. It is the best day of the year. (Rice +2)

choices.text: Give each family something back

effects.log: You give each family something back from your Belly in exchange: a good pot, a plough, a hinge. The festival is much longer after that, and much louder. (Rice +2)

events.text: A scholar is writing a true history of you and has come with a brush and a great deal of paper: {npc}, who wants to know, before anything else, what you ate first.

choices.text: Say: a needle

effects.log: "A needle," you say. {npc} writes it down, and waits for more, and you tell the rest, from the first grain onward. It takes a year. The history is very long and almost entirely true. (Rice +1)

choices.text: Say: a pair of hands, first, before anything

effects.log: "Before the needle," you say, "a pair of hands." {npc} puts the brush down and listens to that part without writing anything at all. (Rice +2)

events.text: {npc}, a famous smith, has come to ask a professional question: what does the best iron taste like? {npc} has made swords for three sects and ploughs for nine villages and has never known.

choices.text: Tell {him} the truth: of the hands that used it

effects.log: "Of the hands that used it," you say. "A plough tastes of the farmer. A sword tastes of the fear." {npc} goes home and makes nothing but ploughs for the rest of {his} life. (Rice +1)

choices.text: Ask {him} for a taste of {his} best work

effects.log: {npc} gives you a hoe, the best work of a lifetime. You eat it, and tell {npc} what it tastes of, in detail. {npc} weeps, which you did not expect, and is very pleased. (Rice +1)

events.text: Pilgrims come up the path to you in spring now, with incense and a few nails each, and leave them at your feet and ask for things: a good harvest, a child's fever gone, someone home safe from the army.

choices.text: Eat the nails and the bad luck with them

effects.log: You eat the nails, and lie outside the pilgrims' houses on the way home and eat what you can of the bad luck. Some of the prayers come true. The pilgrims are very sure it was you. (Rice +2)

choices.text: Tell them you are not a god

effects.log: You tell them you are not a god, only rice and iron. They nod, and leave the nails anyway, and ask for the same things. You do what you can. (Rice +1)

events.text: A pilgrim leaves no nails, only a little bowl of rice and a scrap of paper with a name on it: someone who cannot sleep, in a village a month's walk away.

choices.text: Walk the month to that village

effects.log: You walk the month. At the village you find the house, and lie down outside it, and eat what comes out at night. The name on the paper sleeps. (Rice +3)

choices.text: Eat the rice and send a dream back down the road

effects.log: You cannot walk everywhere. You eat the rice and lie facing that village all night, and something goes down the road from you, softly. Perhaps it arrives. (Rice +1)

events.text: Two thieves have climbed you in the night with a ladder and a rope and are trying to pull a famous hilt out of your hide. They are very quiet, and very bad at it.

choices.text: Let them pull, and then sneeze

effects.log: You let them pull for an hour, and then sneeze. The thieves land in the paddy, the ladder lands on them, and the rope stays in your hide for years as a souvenir.

choices.text: Ask them, quietly, what they need

effects.log: You ask them, very quietly, what they need. Seed rice, it turns out, and a roof. You give them a plain old sword to sell for both, and they climb down speechless. (Rice +2)

events.text: A summer storm, and you are lying on the ridge with a hundred hilts standing up on your back, and the lightning has found them. It strikes you again and again, all night.

choices.text: Eat the lightning

effects.log: You eat it, bolt by bolt. It is fire of a kind, and fire is food. In the morning you glow faintly blue, and the village below says the sky fed you. (Heat +15)

choices.text: Go down off the ridge, like a sensible hill

effects.log: You go down off the ridge and lie in the valley like a sensible hill. The storm grumbles off east. The farmers say it was the first time they saw a mountain move to get out of the rain.

events.text: You sleep a whole century. When you wake, there are pines growing on your back, deer grazing your flank, and a small shrine someone has built on your shoulder, with a bowl of rice in it, fresh.

choices.text: Lie very still so as not to tip the shrine

effects.log: You lie very still, all day, so as not to tip the shrine. In the evening someone comes up and changes the rice. (Rice +2)

choices.text: Get up, carefully, and see what changed

effects.log: You get up, very carefully, with the shrine held level on your shoulder like a tray. The valley has a new road and an old feud and the same rice. You lie down again. (Rice +1)
